name: Doctor On Demand vs Teladoc Health
title: Doctor On Demand vs Teladoc Health: Telehealth Platform Comparison
description: Compare Doctor On Demand (Included Health, 98M+ covered) vs Teladoc Health (90M+ members, BetterHelp). Two major telehealth platforms for virtual care.

summary.bottom_line: Doctor On Demand (now part of Included Health) and Teladoc Health are major telehealth competitors. Doctor On Demand covers 98M+ Americans through employer benefits and emphasizes integrated care navigation. Teladoc is the largest telehealth company (90M+ members, NASDAQ-listed) and owns BetterHelp for therapy. Both offer medical, behavioral health, and chronic care - your employer benefit typically determines which you use.

sections.heading: Employer-Focused Telehealth
sections.content: Both Doctor On Demand and Teladoc primarily reach users through employer benefits. Doctor On Demand merged with Grand Rounds to form Included Health, emphasizing care navigation - helping employees find the right doctors and navigate complex health decisions. Teladoc focuses on comprehensive virtual care delivery and owns BetterHelp for mental health. Your employer's choice typically determines which you access.

sections.heading: Cost Comparison
sections.content: Self-pay pricing is nearly identical: $75 for urgent care, $299 initial psychiatry. The real cost depends on your employer benefit. Many employers cover 100% of telehealth visits through either platform. With insurance, expect $0-50 copays. For therapy, Teladoc's BetterHelp offers subscription pricing ($65-100/week) while Doctor On Demand uses traditional per-session ($100-200).

sections.heading: Care Navigation vs BetterHelp
sections.content: Doctor On Demand's key differentiator through Included Health is care navigation - helping you find specialists, understand treatment options, and coordinate care. Teladoc's differentiator is BetterHelp integration - subscription-based therapy with unlimited messaging. If you need help navigating complex health decisions, Included Health/Doctor On Demand excels. If you want ongoing therapist access, Teladoc/BetterHelp works better.

recommendations.when: Your employer provides Included Health benefits - you get telehealth plus care navigation.
Your employer or insurer provides Teladoc - it's the most widely available platform.
You want subscription-based therapy with unlimited messaging between sessions.
You need help navigating complex health decisions, finding specialists, or understanding treatment options.

faqs.q: Is Doctor On Demand the same as Included Health?
faqs.a: Doctor On Demand merged with Grand Rounds in 2021 to form Included Health. The Doctor On Demand brand continues for telehealth services, while Included Health is the parent company offering broader care navigation.

faqs.q: Which is bigger - Doctor On Demand or Teladoc?
faqs.a: By member count, they're comparable (98M+ vs 90M+). Teladoc is larger by revenue and market presence as a public company. Doctor On Demand/Included Health is employer-focused while Teladoc also has direct-to-consumer channels.

faqs.q: Can I use either without employer benefits?
faqs.a: Yes. Both offer self-pay options ($75 urgent care, $299 psychiatry initial). However, they're designed for employer/insurer distribution. For direct self-pay, platforms like Cerebral or Brightside may be more economical.

faqs.q: Which has better mental health services?
faqs.a: Both offer quality psychiatry and therapy. Teladoc owns BetterHelp with subscription-based therapy including unlimited messaging. Doctor On Demand offers traditional per-session therapy. Choose based on whether you prefer subscription vs per-session models.
